title: zygmuntz-classifier-calibration
universal_lens: Calibration maps raw scores to probabilities via three operators: reliability diagram (empirical CDF of scores vs outcomes), Platt scaling (two-parameter logistic map), isotonic regression (pool-adjacent-violators monotone projection). The selector routes by calibration-set size n: Platt for n < n*, isotonic for n ≥ n*, with reliability diagram as invariant QC layer.
gsi_mapping: GSI treats calibration as conformal prediction: reliability diagram computes empirical coverage per score bin; Platt scaling yields parametric predictive distribution; isotonic regression gives nonparametric conditional quantile map. The selector enforces finite-sample validity: small-n uses parametric shrinkage, large-n uses empirical process, both guarded by diagram QC.
gse_mapping: GSE state-transition: raw model score → calibrated probability → decision threshold. Platt provides smooth differentiable transition for gradient-based control; isotonic provides piecewise-constant transition for discrete action spaces. Reliability diagram monitors distributional shift: if W1-4 diagram diverges from 2025 baseline, recalibration trigger fires.

primitives.name: Reliability Diagram QC Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Vision The canonical minimal demo of the three classical calibration tools: reliability diagrams (accuracy-vs-confidence plots), Platt's scaling (sigmoid fit on scores), and isotonic regression (nonparametric monotonic fit) — shown on a random forest over the Adult dataset.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: k: bin index (dimensionless); n_k: samples in bin k (count); acc_k = (1/n_k) Σ_{i∈bin_k} y_i (dimensionless); conf_k = (1/n_k) Σ_{i∈bin_k} f_i (dimensionless); diagram plots (conf_k, acc_k) for k=1..K
primitives.assumptions: Bins partition [0,1] score range; sufficient samples per bin for empirical accuracy estimate; held-out set independent of training
primitives.breakdown_regime: Empty or near-empty bins (n_k → 0) cause infinite variance; adversarial binning can hide miscalibration; diagram only detects marginal calibration, not conditional

layer2.mapping: GSI: empirical coverage plot for conformal prediction; GSE: distributional shift monitor — if (conf_k, acc_k) trajectory deviates from identity line beyond tolerance, recalibration triggered
layer2.telemetry: Maximum absolute deviation max_k |acc_k - conf_k|; integrated calibration error Σ_k (n_k/N) |acc_k - conf_k|

primitives.name: Platt Sigmoid Calibration Map
primitives.verbatim_quote: Vision The canonical minimal demo of the three classical calibration tools: reliability diagrams (accuracy-vs-confidence plots), Platt's scaling (sigmoid fit on scores), and isotonic regression (nonparametric monotonic fit) — shown on a random forest over the Adult dataset.
primitives.latex: P(y=1 | f) = \frac{1}{1 + \exp(A f + B)} \quad \text{where } A,B = \arg\min_{A,B} \sum_i \log(1 + \exp(-y_i'(A f_i + B))), \; y_i' = 2y_i - 1
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: f: raw classifier score (dimensionless, typically log-odds or margin); A: slope parameter (dimensionless); B: intercept parameter (dimensionless); P: calibrated probability (dimensionless, [0,1])
primitives.assumptions: Scores follow logistic distribution conditional on class; two-parameter family sufficient; calibration set i.i.d. from deployment distribution
primitives.breakdown_regime: Small calibration sets (n < 50) cause high variance in A,B; multimodal score distributions violate logistic assumption; extreme scores (|f| → ∞) saturate to 0/1 regardless of true probability

layer2.mapping: GSI: parametric predictive distribution for Bayesian updating; GSE: differentiable transition kernel for gradient-based policy optimization — ∂P/∂f = A P(1-P) enables backprop through calibration
layer2.telemetry: Negative log-likelihood on held-out set; Brier score decomposition (reliability + resolution + uncertainty)

primitives.name: Isotonic Regression Calibration Map
primitives.verbatim_quote: Vision The canonical minimal demo of the three classical calibration tools: reliability diagrams (accuracy-vs-confidence plots), Platt's scaling (sigmoid fit on scores), and isotonic regression (nonparametric monotonic fit) — shown on a random forest over the Adult dataset.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: f_i: raw score (dimensionless); y_i ∈ {0,1}: label (dimensionless); g: monotone calibration map (dimensionless, [0,1]); n: calibration set size (count)
primitives.assumptions: True calibration map is monotone non-decreasing; calibration set i.i.d.; sufficient data to avoid overfitting (n ≫ number of distinct score values)
primitives.breakdown_regime: Small n causes overfit: PAVA memorizes calibration set (step function with many jumps); non-monotone true relationship violates assumption; extrapolation beyond score range undefined

layer2.mapping: GSI: nonparametric conditional quantile map for distribution-free inference; GSE: piecewise-constant transition for discrete action spaces — each constant segment maps to a decision region
layer2.telemetry: Number of PAVA pools (effective degrees of freedom); held-out Brier score vs Platt; calibration error on temporal holdout (W1-4 vs 2025)

primitives.name: Calibration Policy Selector
primitives.verbatim_quote: **REBUILD** as a two-line policy: Platt for small-n signals, isotonic for large-n signals, reliability diagram attached to every row.
primitives.latex: \text{Select } \mathcal{M} = \begin{cases} \text{Platt} & n < n^* \\ \text{Isotonic} & n \ge n^* \end{cases} \quad \text{with } n^* \approx 200 \text{ (empirical)}, \; \text{always attach reliability diagram}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: n: calibration set size (count); n*: threshold (count, ~200); M: selected calibration operator (categorical); diagram: reliability diagram (QC artifact)
primitives.assumptions: Threshold n* balances bias-variance: Platt has higher bias lower variance, isotonic has lower bias higher variance; reliability diagram detects both miscalibration and distribution shift
primitives.breakdown_regime: Wrong threshold n* causes systematic over/under-fitting; diagram omitted → silent calibration failure; non-stationary deployment invalidates held-out assumption

layer2.mapping: GSI: model selection via finite-sample risk bound; GSE: meta-controller that switches calibration regime based on data budget — small-n regime uses parametric shrinkage for stability, large-n regime uses empirical flexibility
layer2.telemetry: Regret vs oracle selector; calibration error on temporal holdout; diagram divergence metric (W1-4 vs 2025)

reasoning_traces.think:
The three calibration operators form a hierarchy of flexibility: reliability diagram (nonparametric diagnostic), Platt (parametric map, 2 DoF), isotonic (nonparametric map, O(n) DoF). The selector implements structural risk minimization: for small n, the parametric Platt's bias is preferable to isotonic's variance; for large n, isotonic's consistency dominates. The reliability diagram is the invariant QC layer — it measures the same quantity (marginal calibration error) regardless of which map is used. Failure modes: (1) isotonic overfit when n < distinct scores → step function memorizes noise; (2) Platt misspecification when true map non-logistic → irreducible bias; (3) diagram silence when bins too coarse → hidden miscalibration. The temporal guard (2025 vs W1-4 diagram comparison) detects covariate shift: if score distribution shifts, marginal calibration breaks even if conditional calibration holds. This is the conformal prediction insight: marginal coverage ≠ conditional coverage. The selector must be wired into the GSE state machine as a pre-decision calibration gate.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: Platt (1999) derived sigmoid fit for SVM outputs; Zadrozny & Elkan (2001) generalized to isotonic regression via PAVA (Barlow et al. 1972); reliability diagrams trace to Murphy & Winkler (1977) forecast verification. The two-line policy distills 30 years of calibration literature into an operational rule: parametric for scarcity, nonparametric for abundance, always verify. Retrocausal Genealogy: Rooted in zygmuntz-classifier-calibration (f81f5e6088bc5bad), this derivation preserves strict unit consistency, explicit validity boundaries, zero-leakage temporal separation, and bounded structural integration across GSI calibration heads, spectral orthogonalization clusters, and GSE Stage-2 situational reasoning families without fabricating parameters.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Opposing agent is the deployment environment that shifts score distributions. The model trainer assumes i.i.d. calibration set; the environment violates this via concept drift. The reliability diagram is the detector: if the environment shifts P(f), the diagram's (conf_k, acc_k) points move off-diagonal. The selector's threshold n* is a bet on data abundance — if the environment starves calibration data (small n), Platt's shrinkage protects; if environment floods data (large n), isotonic's flexibility exploits. The diagram attached to every row is the audit trail for adversarial review.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Veto conditions: (1) isotonic selected but n < 50 → veto, force Platt (overfit risk); (2) reliability diagram shows max|acc-conf| > 0.1 on any bin → veto deployment, trigger recalibration; (3) W1-4 diagram KL-divergence from 2025 baseline > threshold → veto, distribution shift detected; (4) Platt and isotonic disagree on held-out set by > 0.05 Brier → veto, model misspecification. Anti-collinearity: calibration set must be disjoint from training and test; leakage from using test labels for calibration invalidates all guarantees.
